column1: # Every topic of the stack, in one place. create-topics.sh reads this file.
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   name             the topic name
#   partitions       how many pieces the topic is split into; more
#                    partitions means more consumers can read it at the
#                    same time
#   retention_hours  how long a message stays before Kafka deletes it;
#                    "-" means use KAFKA_RETENTION_HOURS (the default)
#   key              what the producer uses as the message key, so that
#                    all messages about one entity keep their order
#   purpose          a short note for humans
# Replication is always 3 (one copy per broker) and is set by the script.
# Partition counts re-derived for NYC TLC real-scale fleet/demand (~106,000
# licensed vehicles, ~655,000 trips/day full-scale - see h-bootstrap's own
# scale settings): driver_location/rider_location carry by far the most
# messages and scale with fleet size, so they get the most headroom for
# consumer parallelism (cache-updater, clickhouse-sink) if those services
# are ever run as more than one instance. trip_requests/trip_lifecycle scale
# with request volume, which stays modest even at full scale (well under
# 1,000 messages/minute) - some headroom, not as much. city_hotspots is
# capped at 263 possible keys (one per real TLC zone) regardless of fleet
# or demand scale, so it stays at one partition per broker.
# dispatch_offers is the one topic that does not size with an entity count
# or with trip volume: it carries one message per offer, and a request can
# be offered to several drivers before one accepts. Its volume is trip
# volume multiplied by offers-per-match, which is a marketplace property
# nobody can predict from the outside - it rises exactly when supply is
# short, which is also when everything else is busiest. Six partitions
# matches trip_lifecycle for now; the real ratio is measured at mid scale
# before the full-scale run and this number revisited then, not guessed
# harder now.
# retention_hours overrides exist because one default never fit every
# topic here once real scale was actually flowing: driver_location alone
# at full scale (~106,000 drivers, ~60% online, one report every
# DRIVER_TICK_SECONDS) is on the order of 20,000 messages/second - the
# 48-hour default this project used to apply everywhere would let it grow
# toward several hundred GB per broker (every broker holds a full replica
# at replication factor 3 with exactly 3 brokers), more than this host's
# whole data disk. Cut down here to what real full-scale volume can
# actually afford to keep; the low-volume topics keep the long default,
# since nothing about their size demands otherwise.
# The cdc.* topics are NOT listed here: Debezium creates them itself, one
# per PostgreSQL table (see d-infra-debezium).
# ksql_* and _confluent-ksql-* are not listed here either, for the same
# reason: ksqlDB creates the sink topic of every table in ksql/*.sql, plus
# its own command topic and each query's internal state, and owns their
# settings. Adding one here would mean two things creating the same topic
# with two ideas about its partitions.
# name
driver_location
column5: where each driver is, every few seconds

column1: rider_location
column5: where each rider's phone is during a trip

column1: trip_requests
column5: a passenger asks for a ride

column1: trip_lifecycle
column5: every status change of a trip, up to the final fare

column1: dispatch_offers
column5: every offer dispatch made, and what the driver said

column1: city_hotspots
column5: demand score per city zone, published by city-service

column1: segment_traffic_updates
column5: a real congestion-factor update, published by city-service
